rules: Pier, shore, harbor, stream/tributary, and boat/offshore evidence are separate fishing modes; one mode never raises another mode's rating without direct support.
A legal year-round season establishes legality, not a year-round Good or Fair PierCast opportunity.
A zero outside a survey's sampled months is not evidence of biological absence.
Port-, county-, or citywide evidence can bound timing but cannot be represented as an exact-structure catch rate.
Daily curve knots remain model judgments because the reviewed agencies generally publish seasonal or monthly evidence, not daily pier catch probability.

sources.title: Wisconsin fishing report 2026 — Great Lakes salmon and trout
sources.mode: Regional Lake Michigan/Green Bay open water, tributary, and shore context; passages are kept mode-specific.
sources.finding: Brown trout fishing is year-round; early spring is a major nearshore period. Adults are collected each fall at Kewaunee, Root, and Milwaukee, with eggs taken in November and early December. The report identifies late-September-through-winter shore opportunity in major tributaries.
sources.limits: It does not publish daily city-pier catch rates. Green Bay, tributary, and trolling statements cannot be copied to every Lake Michigan pier.

sources.title: Fabulous year of fishing
sources.mode: Regional harbor, river-mouth, nearshore, and pier timing.
sources.finding: The agency describes a strong open-water winter harbor/river-mouth brown-trout fishery and explicitly says brown trout are available to Lake Michigan pier anglers in August.
sources.limits: Statewide month guidance establishes a prior, not equal strength at every port.

sources.title: Wisconsin's 2024 Open Water Sportfishing Effort and Harvest From Lake Michigan and Green Bay
sources.mode: Pier and shore tables separated from boat modes.
sources.finding: Pier brown-trout harvest is strongly spring-weighted in 2024.
sources.limits: East-shore direct sampling ran May-September; spring was modeled and October pier/shore estimates were omitted. The table therefore cannot prove October absence.

sources.title: Lake Michigan Creel Harvest Tables 1998-2024
sources.mode: County-by-mode recurrence; pier column used and boat columns excluded.
sources.finding: Brown-trout pier harvest recurs across the Wisconsin counties and supports differing port ceilings.
sources.limits: County rows can pool ports and do not provide directed species effort.

sources.title: Close to Home Fishing Opportunities
sources.mode: Named pier, breakwall, harbor, and shore access/species inventory.
sources.finding: Confirms target identity and access geography at named Wisconsin structures.
sources.limits: Species lists do not quantify season, effort, or catch rate.

sources.title: Creel Sportfishing Estimates dashboard — preserved Pier/Dock extracts
sources.mode: Monthly port Pier/Dock estimates; other fishing modes excluded from magnitude decisions.
sources.finding: Supports recurrence, month-level shape, and relative port strength for the listed Michigan cities.
sources.limits: Coverage varies by port, month, and year; port rows may pool multiple structures and all-species effort is not directed brown-trout effort.

sources.title: Roadmap to Fishing Lake Michigan — accessible version
sources.mode: Port-level seasonal guide; fishing modes mixed.
sources.finding: Corroborates winter/spring brown-trout windows across western Lake Michigan and a fall brown-trout lead at Whitehall.
sources.limits: It is not an exact-pier catch-rate source and some ports are grouped.

sources.title: Roadmap to Fishing Lake Huron — accessible version
sources.mode: Port-level seasonal lead; fishing modes mixed.
sources.finding: Provides seasonal port context used only with Pier/Dock or exact-city corroboration.
sources.limits: Blank cells are not absence; port-level occurrence cannot set a pier score by itself.

sources.title: Better Fishing Waters
sources.finding: Confirms brown trout as a target at named or grouped pier fisheries.
sources.limits: Does not quantify season or catch rate; some ports are grouped.

sources.title: Central Lake Michigan Management Unit
sources.finding: Directly supports fall and spring brown-trout fishing in the Muskegon channel/pier setting.
sources.limits: Qualitative management guidance, not a daily catch-rate series.

sources.publisher: Illinois Natural History Survey / Illinois Department of Natural Resources
sources.title: Survey of Sport Fishing in the Illinois Portion of Lake Michigan, 2024
sources.mode: Pedestrian site estimates, kept separate from boat modes.
sources.finding: Directly records spring brown trout at Chicago's Montrose site and supports cold-season Illinois shore opportunity with the multi-year site program.
sources.limits: Seasonal sampling does not cover every winter month or every structure; survey zeroes outside coverage are not absence.

sources.title: Fishing Areas
sources.mode: Citywide shore, harbor dock, and pier access/timing.
sources.finding: Supports year-round access context and the city's broad species calendar.
sources.limits: Citywide timing cannot be treated as a Montrose- or Navy-Pier-specific catch rate.

sources.title: Fishing in Lake Michigan and tributaries
sources.mode: Seasonal shore, pier, tributary, and offshore guidance with each passage kept separate.
sources.finding: Identifies brown trout at winter shore discharges, in spring nearshore catches, and during fall returns to stocking sites; summer salmonids are described offshore.
sources.limits: The fall passage combines pier and stream availability and supplies no directed catch rate.
